title: Admin Lambda Runbooks & Support Automation Gateway
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Build a lightweight, auditable gateway that exposes vetted admin runbooks as small serverless functions ("runbook lambdas"). The gateway should allow support engineers to execute common operational tasks via the Console, the admin CLI, or Slack actions while enforcing RBAC, dry-run, idempotency, and automatic audit logging to our security ledger. Goal is to reduce incident-to-resolution time for common operational workflows and remove manual step-checking in high-frequency tasks.
motivation: Current Confluence runbooks and ad-hoc scripts are slow to discover, hard to automate, and often require manual copy/paste of commands. By converting high-value runbooks into small, parameterized functions with structured outputs and guarded execution, we improve speed, reduce human error, and create traceable audit trails for compliance.
acceptance_criteria: Create runtime and deployable format for runbook lambdas (YAML metadata + single entrypoint) that supports dry-run and verbose logging
Admin Console can list available runbook lambdas with descriptions, required permissions, and example parameters
Runbook execution requires RBAC check; unauthorized attempts are rejected and logged
Each execution emits a structured audit event to the security ledger (requester, params masked, runbook id, result, artifacts links)
Runbooks support idempotent flags and safe-mode to avoid destructive actions during incidents
CLI and Slack integration: runbook can be executed from opsctl and via Slack slash action with approval flow
Provide migration tooling to convert 10 high-ROI Confluence runbooks into lambda format and include at least 3 unit/integration tests per function
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Spec & schema for runbook lambda format + RBAC model integration (2 sprints)
Phase 2: Gateway service with execution queue, retry policy, and audit emitter (1 sprint)
Phase 3: Console UI + CLI bindings + Slack adapter (1 sprint)
Phase 4: Migrate initial runbook set, testing, and security review (1 sprint)
Phase 5: Rollout and monitoring: metrics dashboard for runbook latency, success rate, and invocation patterns
technical_notes: Runbook lambda format should be single-file with frontmatter: id, description, inputs, output-schema, required_permissions, safe_mode true/false
Implement execution sandbox to validate inputs against JSON schema and mask secrets using KMS before logging
Use existing ops-worker pool for short-running tasks; long-running jobs should spawn transient worker VMs with annotated runbook id
Audit events posted to /internal/security/ledger with envelope versioning to support future schema changes
Retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter; non-idempotent runbooks default to manual retry only
Expose a dry-run mode that returns planned actions without mutating state and emits an explicit "dry-run" audit event
security_review_feedback: Security: require two-step approval for any runbook that modifies infra tags or billing-related resources
Add rate limits on runbook execution per-identity to avoid blast radius from compromised accounts
Ensure runbook artifacts and logs are TTL'd and accessible only to approved roles
ux_review_feedback: Console should surface required permissions inline and show example parameter values
Include an inline preview for dry-run results and links to the underlying Confluence runbook for context
Slack integration needs to show the runbook id and have an optional comment field for auditability
